title: Backend pytest compatibility test hard-requires npm build tooling
reasoning: A backend pytest module unconditionally shells out to `npm run build` under `packages/windie-sdk-js` and then runs a Node ESM script. That makes the Python backend test suite depend on Node, npm, installed JS dependencies, and a successful SDK build even when the test command for this feature is simply pytest. In Python-only CI, backend-only developer loops, or environments where npm deps have not been installed, these tests fail before exercising the backend schemas they are meant to validate.
reproduction: Run `pytest tests/backend/test_sdk_runtime_backend_compatibility.py` in an environment with Python dependencies installed but without Node/npm or without `packages/windie-sdk-js` dependencies installed; collection/execution will fail from the subprocess calls rather than from a backend compatibility assertion.
recommendation: Gate this as an explicit integration test or add a clear skip when Node/npm or the SDK package dependencies are unavailable. If backend pytest must remain self-contained, replace the live npm build with checked-in fixture payloads plus a separate SDK CI job that regenerates or validates those fixtures.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test itself is the hazard: it validates the happy path only when JS tooling is present and does not cover the backend-test environment missing that tooling.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small test around the helper or marker behavior that verifies the compatibility test is skipped with an actionable reason when the SDK build prerequisites are unavailable.
minimumFixScope: tests/backend/test_sdk_runtime_backend_compatibility.py and the relevant pytest marker/CI selection for SDK compatibility tests.
